plain_english: Margaret Glasgow, sometime wife of John Easton, died intestate in December, apparently 1578. Her estate was administered later; 8 November 1580 is the marginal confirmation date, not her death date.

Cuthbert Kaddell/Keddell of the same provisionally read residence is expressly called her son in the opening. The confirmation again calls him son of the deceased Margaret and calls Margaret his mother. These kinship phrases independently establish their mother-son relationship; executor appointment alone is not the basis.

The inventory records livestock, six bolls of oats, household furnishings and clothing. Debts receivable include James Easton and Michael Mertyn. A debt to Roland Dundas concerns a year's teind. Those financial connections do not establish kinship.

The totals are consistent with the earlier reading of goods at 47 pounds 14 shillings 8 pence; receivables 10 pounds 10 shillings; gross estate 58 pounds 4 shillings 8 pence; debts payable 20 shillings; net estate 57 pounds 4 shillings 8 pence; and one half as the deceased's portion. Individual numeral forms remain marked provisional in the working lines rather than silently supplied from the arithmetic.
findings: Image 355, opening lines 6-10: 'sumtyme spous to Johne estoun' and 'hir sone' identify different relationships. The son's surname is not Easton in the supplied reading; John Easton's paternity is not stated.
Image 356, confirmation lines 32 and 36-37: 'sone to the said vmqle Margaret' and 'his mother' independently confirm the maternity stated in the opening.
Image 355: the upper estate and its confirmation end before the new Margaret heading and lower opening. Names from that preceding estate must not be attributed to Margaret's household or executors.
Image 356, lines 12-18: the deduction and division support an estate-account reading, not an additional family distribution identifying another child.
The complete two-image span specified by the digital header is supplied and has been visually examined. Coverage is full, but substantial confirmation formula and some figures remain unresolved.
changes_from_previous: Freshly confirms the material mother-son conclusion and the prohibition on changing Cuthbert's surname to Easton without independent evidence.
Confirms the preceding-estate boundary on image 355 and the distinction between death and confirmation dates.
The older aggregate account reading is compatible with the supplied images, but several numeral shapes remain provisional in this new literal working reading.
A focused reread improves two associate names from bracketed readings to Michael Mertyn and Roland Dundas; neither is assigned a family relationship.
The appointment decree day is left unresolved here; the older tentative [16?] October reading is not independently confirmed.
Separates line-oriented manuscript wording from modern interpretation and from the older formatted ledger table. No older narrative has been presented as if it were a fresh literal transcription.
unresolved: The index confirms Croftmalloch. The manuscript's individual strokes remain provisionally rendered Croftmelloch[?], without weakening the confirmed indexed place wording.
Confirm the death-year and inventory numeral forms, livestock quantities, and the October appointment day.
The cautioner's name and substantial portions of the confirmation formula need another palaeographic pass.
The record does not identify Cuthbert's father.
confidence_statement: Both PDF pages were rendered at 170 dpi and visually examined, with enlarged crops for the opening, accounts and confirmation; prior saved readings were consulted only after the initial fresh image pass. High confidence in the three mother-son expressions and document boundaries; moderate confidence in dates/aggregate accounts; low confidence in some names, figures and legal formula. Full coverage describes the supplied span, not a fully resolved diplomatic edition. Original spellings are retained where legible; superscripts are lowered and uncertain expansions bracketed.
